Battery acid is available at auto parts stores as well, and it's usually 95% sulfuric acid with some additives to help it work as a battery.

We have a cherry blossom tree in our yard that my wife loves. She wants me to take a cutting from it and start another tree. Here's the question:
What's the best way to ensure success?

Thanks!

I've had the best luck with hardwood cuttings. About mid summer, take a good foot long section of last years growth. Cut the bottom right below one of the leaf nodes, and leave it long enough to have four or five nodes above that. Mix up some sand and perlite in a container that you can close. I use a deep tupperware. Get it wet enough that it clumps, but not so wet that there is standing water in the bottom. Mix the bottom of the cutting in rooting hormone and stick it in the 'soil'. Close the container up and leave it on a sunny windowsill. Open it once a day for an hour or so to let it air out or you will get mold, and mist it every now and then to keep the cutting moist.

I would suggest taking a dozen or so cuttings and planting them in a large container together.
